It was beautiful, well maintained, loved it.

Trail was easy to navigate. Wished people picked up after their dogs. Lookout was closed off at the falls during winter.
This is not appropriate for cross country skiing. Maybe in fresh snow cutting your own trail,  even then some of the hills and switchbacks require better than average skills.
Absolutely beautiful today! Loads of snow! Path was well trodden in most parts. Not many people out there today w it being -10C

on a day like today. It is definitely advisable to wear crampons. The ice can become very treacherous in certain areas as there are some pretty steep hills in areas of the trail. The Falls were both lovely to see. If you want to be down at the base of Swayze Falls, you need to find a way down before you get to the observation deck because there is no way to get down from there. Even with the icy conditions I was quite surprised to see a handful of trail runners. And there were quite a few dogs, enjoying the trails as well. So it is manageable, but if you don’t have great balance or don’t do well and ice it can be quite treacherous.
Super muddy, but not impossible
Very muddy today, but to be expected
The trail is in great shape.
Very well marked trail. The inclines were very slippery with mud. Some trees on trail.

Some of the inclines were extremely slippery with mud. Seems like the trail is mainly for mountain biking based on the shape of parts of the trail. Would good back when the trails are less muddy to explore other parts.
nicely marked, great views trail through multiple landscapes make for an enjoyable med-long distance hike! few inclines and wet spots.

I hiked this trail today and had an amazing experience. The scenery was beautiful, with gorgeous views and plenty of wildlife along the way. I even saw a woman riding a horse, which added to the peaceful atmosphere. The trail is in great condition, with some steep hills that are manageable and make the hike interesting. A fun note..there’s a waterfall at the end, but it’s seasonal, so you may or may not catch it. Overall, a serene and enjoyable hike with lots to see!
Great trail conditions, still beautiful fall colors, and just plain scenic!
Not too muddy, no water flowing right now though, still pretty with all the fall colours
Will be very lovely in the fall!
Perfect conditions today. Waterfall is dry though!
First half is completely overgrown. Fun if you like bushwhacking.
Lots of winding hills, dry and easy to follow :)

Lots of horse poop as horses go on the Swayze falls trail aka blue/yellow trail/white trails. A few steep hills but mostly flat grounds, beautiful waterfalls and creeks, beautiful view in open fields, mild ticks but not bad.
Drier trails than I’ve seen for Swayze in a while. People were courteous, and most dogs were leashed.
Nice relatively easy trail

I went on this trail when it had been raining for several days. I still had a great time and the waterfall was beautiful, with the information panel being very interesting. But I definitely only recommend going in dry conditions!
Awesomeness!!!
Muddy!

With extremely muddy conditions it took about 2.5hrs, with minimal stops. 
Waterfall is located near the trailhead if you start counter-clockwise. Variety of short steep sections and large open sections.
Too muddy
muddy as FARK but so pretty!!!
Muddy conditions in March.
It's not a bad hike, just bad timing. Extreme muddy conditions with some ice still, but the massive ruts in the trail make the water difficult to traverse.
Snow packed, but rain on its way. Anyone hiking tomorrow may need crampons.
Best with some kind of icers or crampons on your boots. Trail can be slippery and icey
Average of -5°C the past three days so some slick ice at parts. Frozen footprints can be sharp. Fun and not crowded today.
Icy right now but not crowded and a great trail. Well marked.
A few muddy sections today

There were a few muddy patches along the route, even though it hadn’t rained for a week. Trail runs through shady wooded areas and sunny fields, so remember sun screen!

Most cyclists were courteous and communicated well. All dogs we saw were leashed. Beautiful day to enjoy the fall foliage, although many trees were already bare. The air smelled fantastic (“autumn spice” haha).

Extremely muddy today. My tread filled with mud which made it difficult to continue. It poured rain all night last night, so I’m sure on average it’s not too bad. Made for a more interesting adventure!
Beautiful trail, with only 1 steep section
Nature is the Best
Meant to do the Swayze falls trail but ended up going down a different one, but it was enjoyable!
A beautiful hike. As other people have mentioned, the waterfall currently is very small. Hearing the bees, birds, and seeing two small fawns were highlights of the trail
Trails 4 & 5 have super mud puddles at the moment but still passable.

Nice loop rewards
Ed with a beautiful waterfall.
Dry no waterfall
loved this trail over all but at this destination there is a mental wire across the path Proceed with caution
Overgrown weedy areas, muddy in some areas, but manageable.
Fairly well maintained.  Route is well marked.  Parking pretty limited so come early.  Not too many people though.

Some muddy sections, well marked generally but turnoffs not identified. Primarily forest and if done clockwise, scenic views at the end. Horses can sneak up on you so watch out and make sure that you don’t become their next meal(I hear they eat hikers when there are no carrots around so you may want to bring a few… or bring sugar cubes)
From open weed fields to wooden trails. Parts are nice and parts are well you know. Not crowded. Trails can be muddy. Wear good shoes!!
grown in. to many tics

MUDDY! But very much expected considering the skies opened up and downpoured on us a few times during the hike. No complaints from us tho, added to the adventure! Had the best time, with the best company! But take extreme caution if you go in the rain, my fiance did fall…twice
Very muddy and one bridge is washed out. Otherwise a good hike

This trail provided just the right amount of challenge and elevation gain to kick off the summer hiking season. However, be prepared for muddy and slippery conditions on about half of the trail. Hiking boots and poles are highly recommended for a safe and enjoyable experience.
Great trail but muddy sections this time of year.  Only reason for the 4 stars,  rest of the year this is a five star trail!

simple clean and not busy

A really nice hike with lots of mildly challenging hills. Some muddy areas but not too bad.  The bee activity was so lively in one of the high fields that you could hear all the buzzing! Lots of butterflies too.
Very muddy. Had to turn around.
overgrown on the single track portions. nice trail with a few steep climbs.

Short Hills is pretty nice. 

I ended up getting on the bruce trail via the Swayze Falls trail so I didn't  get to see much of the park. Especially because I didnt know this park didnt close at 8 pm. I eneded up rushing back for no reason.

 It looks like the sprayed alot of pesticides in certain area though. The water fall is nice. That trail down the hill right after the waterfall, lots of thorns after the creek and really overgrown the farther you go. 

Recommend long pants and long sleeves for this park.

Not muddy at all. Very lush and green. There is no water in the falls at the moment.

We went on this trail yesterday. The river is currently dried up and some of the trails are pretty rough. Make sure you’re protecting yourself from ticks! 

Overall, even with the river dried up, the trails were not muddy but definitely want a good pair of hiking boots if you’ve got them.
Black walnut had lots of cracked mud and pitted horse hoof indents. Swayze falls was in a bit better riding shape. Rough run out there right now.
Trail is beautiful, but oh BOY are there ticks! My husband got 10 on him, our dog had 4 and I luckily had 0 (kudos polyester workout pants!) just a heads up!!
Beautiful day and gorgeous hike. Not very shaded so it was hot. Waterfall just a trick but still Beautiful.  Especially from the bottom.

Great trail! We decided to do this trail clockwise and it was fantastic. Well maintained for the most part (a few overgrown sections and a little muddy). But beware, there are LOTS of ticks this season! Be sure to check yourself for ticks and have fun :) 

Note: Swayze Falls is also nicknamed  Dry Falls as it's dry most of the year except after a heavy rainfall or during the Spring melt. The winter freeze gives a spectacular view!
Some muddy areas and trees down across the trail but overall quite dry, well maintained and not many bugs out!
Awsome hike today. No bugs! Happy Victoria Day!

Lots of fun. Very bumpy from dried mud and lots of roots and ruts. A couple of muddy spots but not as bad as it could be after rain.  Some challenging vertical sections I had to walk.  Had to traverse four felled trees. Would like to return when the trees are removed. Some flat field sections to relax on before the next challenges.
Trails are very muddy and can be slippery when it’s been raining. Watch for coyotes.
Good conditions and drying up nicely. There are a few spots of mud, but it is easy to navigate around. Gorgeous April weather!
Weird the app stopped recording 5 minutes into hike and it wasn't until I checked my progress that I noticed. Good hike anyway.

So slippery and muddy

No water on waterfall at present. One bridge is closed but you can bypass the bridge as there is no water in creek. Trails in great condition. Fall colours starting to come out.
Beautiful colours in the fall. No waterfall currently.

Definitely muddy as mentioned (I went in runners and was slipping a fair bit). Otherwise well marked, good split between tree cover and open field. You hit the waterfall early on so just a bit anti-climactic afterwards. All things considered, a good 2 ish hour hike

Nice trail overall! SLots of overgrowth in September which meant I destroyed 100s of beautiful spider webs!!  I’d recommend pants, especially for kids, if you do the full route. Hiking down into the gorge is definitely not for beginners. Trail markers are extremely confusing here, I wouldn’t rely on them, I used maps several times.
Very nice- a tad hilly but manageable. Quite muddy and slippery as lots of clay. Beautiful falls
Great hike but end of the trail bridge was out so shimmed across.

Pretty interesting. I went off the beaten trail and I found a Deer, some turkey's and a boring raccoon!

All in all, Great Park! Although I barely even scratch the surface.

Beware of ticks, particularly if you have a dog. My dog sniffed around the grass at the side of the trail once in a while but for the most part stayed on the path. He came out completely infested with ticks. I’ve never seen anything like it. I believe they were all American dog ticks, so not Lyme carriers but also not harmless.
great trail is fine little mud

Lots of sunny spots with no shade- note to self wear sunscreen next time. LOTS of incline. Also my short little legs did the hike in 2 hours. Still super pretty with beautiful floors.
Trail was well kept, some horse manure but easily avoidable, not the most exciting trail but a nice experience
Great trail, just the right amount of climbing. The falls were dry but the scenery was beautiful.
Ever felt like wanting to visit prison? Bike ride is a must! Would ride again!
very nice hiking place，well done！

EXTREMELY muddy. If you are thinking about taking these trails you will need boots. Lots and lots of muddy spots with lots of difficulty to get through the mud and water. Lots of horse poop to move around.

some muddy spots but aside from that the trail is a real nice walk. will explore more of the park another day.

The first half of this trail was a breeze (left side of loop) the 2nd half is where things went bad. The trail was so overgrown. It was hard to know where the trail was and wasn’t. Some how I ended up on a former trail that is now closed, didn’t know this until I was off it and seen a sign.

Did the walk in September and my fluffy dog got a lot of little burs in his fur.  Otherwise, the walk was very nice but keep your eyes open about half way when the this trail branches off from main trail.   Creek and waterfall are dried up this time of year.

Would be good trail for biking, however, as a walking trail it is not the most beautiful. Lots of walking through open fields, lots of power lines in view. We walked with our 6 month year old and it was tough to be in the sun so long. We prefer more covered trails with larger trees.
Dry falls; otherwise as expected (great!)
Great！very relaxing and soothing trail
Trail flooded partway through- had to turn around

Great trail if you don't mind climbing some downed branches and closed-in bushes. It was quite beautiful despite that. I would not recommend visiting in the rain/after a rain unless you are very good at walking on slippery trails. It's mostly packed clay, so as long as you're sure-footed you'll be fine. Not good for blind dogs (I brought mine and he struggled greatly). My other dog loved it. If you visit with horses, note that there are some steep hills so if your horse struggles with hills, beware. There were neat hitching post/outdoor tie spots for horses as well as the odd picnic table. My dogs loved when we finally made it to the creek. Lots of different terrain to tackle.

Good  trail.  Dog friendly. Fairly easy, some muddy parts.  At the end (if you go clockwise from Roland Rd) there is a steep climb down to Swayze Falls.  Recommend rapelling down if you're looking for something a little more difficult!

A very nice trail. Feels a bit long and there are some rockier, uneven areas but still manageable. Dog friendly. A mix of field walking closer to the end and forested areas too. Not much wildlife except the odd squirrel or chipmunk. Lots of moths and butterflies out
had to see what's it like last time I was in there was 10 years ago.

A great trail with some moderate inclines and mixed terrain. NOTE* did this while the trails were extremely muddy and there were many spots where traction on a descent was a serious concern. Boots were caked and weighed an extra pound or so after only 2km in - would recommend poles if hiking in muddy conditions.

Hit and miss. Some areas are too close to civilization for peace and quiet, however some areas are very peaceful with great views. A bit hot when in the fields and the bugs were bad today. Lots of hills but not so much that the amateur hiker would have trouble.

I’d like to do it again in the fall when the leaves are changing. We had planned to do the loop but made it to about 2.4 ish KMs. I had my baby in a carrier and just wasn’t comfortable doing the long grass with her. Trail was moderately trafficked.
TONS of horse droppings.
recommend in spring

Easy terrain, but in this cold weather we encountered ice, snow, and quite a bit of mud. The mud and ice were both slippery. Our hiking poles helped keep us from slipping. The Falls were definitely the highlight!
Frequent user I love that location.
Relaxing but still interesting hike .We met Young Common Snapping Turtle (Chelydra serpentina) on the main path to the parking lot .

Good trail with enough changing landscape to keep it interesting. Lots of horse droppings so watch your footing. Little more than a trickle coming off of Swayze Falls (hiked in August) but still a very neat rock formation.
Nice trail but can get tricky at points. Swayze Falls were dry
Most of path is covered in brush as it is under used and under regeneration
Enjoyed the area! Came during the spring, so it was quite messy, but enjoyable :) I will be writing a blog post about my trail trek on thecaptainandhislady.com
